item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. The best 2024 evidence shows Khamenei kept the broader political environment loyalist-heavy and only indirectly tolerated a somewhat more technocratic cabinet under Pezeshkian. There is some positive evidence for competent economic staffing, but it looks constrained and mediated, not like Khamenei deliberately empowering independent economic professionals.

The article also says Pezeshkian had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submitting the list. This is the strongest positive sign that a technocratic economic team was at least allowed through, but it is indirect and compromise-driven rather than clear evidence that Khamenei himself prioritized expertise. | 5B.2, 5B.1, 4B.4 |

That supports the view that the system was managing loyalty and legitimacy more than building a serious economic-professional team. | 5B.2, 5B.1, 4B.2 |

**Search Gap**
I found indirect evidence that Khamenei allowed a somewhat more technocratic cabinet to pass, but I did not find a 2024 source showing Khamenei personally appointing a dedicated economic team or directly choosing economic professionals over loyalists. The evidence is mostly about his approval/veto environment and the composition of Pezeshkian’s cabinet, so the best-supported reading is “some constrained technocracy, but not a clear Khamenei-led meritocratic appointment pattern.”
